task.title: Dragging toward an off-screen column doesn't scroll the board horizontally
task.description:
The horizontal sibling of WB-01M004S4ANAEM0Z46HV2914NFK (PR #105), confirmed real during its implementation and review: holding a dragged card at the window's left or right edge leaves [data-board].scrollLeft unchanged, so a card cannot be dragged to a column beyond the current horizontal viewport in one gesture. The fix should reuse PR #105's machinery — the rAF loop, edge zones with a proportional ramp, the sub-pixel carry, and the dragenter/dragDestination acceptance — applied to the board's horizontal scroller, with the same discipline: real-browser proof of the full gesture, loop-leak checks on every termination path, and drop-marker integrity while the board scrolls under a stationary cursor.

## Shipped (2026-08-16, PR #108)

One PR through a two-round adversarial execution-verified review (record on the PR), all browser evidence from real Chrome over CDP.

PR #105's machinery now drives both axes from one rAF loop and one remembered cursor: a shared rate function for the column scroller and the board track, horizontal edge zones of min(72px, 25%) measured from the track's box CLIPPED TO THE WINDOW, separate sub-pixel carries per scroller, the 50ms frame cap, horizontal overshoot past the window edge at full rate (exits through the track's top/bottom stop it), and dragenter/dragover acceptance through dragDestination() preserved. New machinery the sibling story didn't need: releaseDragScroller() lets a column stop scrolling without killing the loop (the track sliding a fresh column under a still cursor is itself what un-hovers the old one), and retargetDragScroller() re-resolves the hovered column every pushing frame via elementFromPoint through the same dragDestination() the drop uses - before it, a card could land in one column while the drop line was drawn in another. Also fixed en route: route changes now retire an active drag (a pre-existing leak left the rAF loop running after navigation), and showPlacement was made idempotent so the drop marker stops churning the DOM under a stationary drag cursor.

The review's blocker was the best catch of the batch: the implementation had removed the window clip after measuring one configuration, but body{min-width:20rem} is rem-based, so a viewport under 20rem - or a normal phone viewport with Chrome's "Very Large" 24px font setting - document-scrolls sideways and puts the edge zone beyond the window: 712px of measured travel collapsing to 0-109px for exactly the readers most likely to have off-screen columns. Restoring the clip fixed every dead case (~700px) and changed none. The review also forced the carry-separation test to genuinely discriminate (the real mutant-killer is a clamped scroller draining a shared accumulator: 0px vs 48px), removed unreproducible churn counts from the record, and un-gated the retarget on clamped tracks. Final matrix: 20 mutations, 20 caught.

Evidence: 6/6+6/6 end-to-end gestures to off-screen columns with one write each, 8/8 mid-scroll releases landing in the line's own column, 134/144 corner frames moving both axes, loop-leak matrix 0/7, deleted column reached at full 1218px travel with tombstone drops intact, baseline 0px confirmed on main. Residuals (accepted): Blink can withdraw its own drop target via a cancel delivering the page nothing - proven unfixable from the page by a three-arm synthetic-event experiment both sides replicated; CDP's low-dragover regime is pessimistic vs a real mouse.
